title: Installing Python

spans.text:
Install Python with the official installer for your operating system from python.org. Windows provides the Python Launcher; macOS and Linux may use a versioned Python 3 command. Reopen the terminal and verify the version after installation.

Windows: use the per-user installer from python.org, enable `Add python.exe to PATH`, and check `py --version`. macOS: use the official macOS installer from python.org; do not replace the system Python, and verify with `python3 --version`. Linux: install `python3`, `python3-venv`, and `python3-pip` through your distribution's package manager; do not remove or replace the system Python. Create a separate virtual environment for each project on all three systems.

spans.code:
# Windows
py --version
py -m pip --version
# macOS and Linux
python3 --version
python3 -m pip --version
Version strings vary by installed Python and pip.

spans.text: Check the version with Python's --version command.

spans.title: Important tip
spans.text: Use `py -m pip` on Windows and `python3 -m pip` on macOS/Linux to install into the intended interpreter.

spans.title: Important detail
spans.text: Installer screens and package names can change; choose a supported Python 3 build for your OS and processor architecture.

spans.title: Warning
spans.text: Do not remove Linux's system Python packages or use `sudo pip install`; OS tools may depend on them.
